summary: Elderly man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on apixaban, HFpEF, PVD s/p aortobifemoral bypass, and CKD stage 3, admitted electively after a scheduled follow-up ERCP performed one month after stent placement for cholangitis. The ERCP demonstrated multiple bile duct stones and sludge; he underwent stent removal, sphincterotomy, and stone/sludge extraction without complication. Post-procedure he was asymptomatic with normal LFTs (ALT 16, AST 23, AlkPhos 102, TBili 1.0) and no leukocytosis, arguing against active cholangitis or post-ERCP pancreatitis. He was observed overnight with apixaban held 48 hours, Lasix briefly held then resumed, and declined inpatient surgical evaluation for cholecystectomy.
most_likely: Choledocholithiasis (bile duct calculi with sludge) treated by ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone extraction

differential.diagnosis: Choledocholithiasis — calculus of bile duct without cholangitis or cholecystitis
supporting_evidence: ERCP showed multiple stones and sludge
Sphincterotomy with stone/sludge extraction and stent removal
Normal bilirubin 1.0, ALT 16, AlkPhos 102 — no active obstruction
opposing_evidence: No current abdominal pain or cholestatic labs
differential.reasoning: The documented ERCP findings of multiple ductal stones and sludge treated with sphincterotomy make bile duct calculi the condition chiefly responsible for this admission.

supporting_evidence: Prior CT/US: mobile gallstones up to 4 mm, gallbladder wall thickening
Surgery recommended CCY if stones found on repeat ERCP
Patient declined surgery, will follow up in clinic
opposing_evidence: No current imaging of the gallbladder this stay
differential.reasoning: Gallbladder stones are documented historically and drive the ongoing cholecystectomy discussion this admission, supporting a secondary code.

differential.diagnosis: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on long-term anticoagulation, apixaban periprocedurally held
supporting_evidence: Continued home propranolol and amiodarone
Apixaban held 2 days pre-procedure, resume 48h post
Prior ICD-10 I480, Z7901
opposing_evidence: Exam RRR; no documented arrhythmia this stay
differential.reasoning: Active chronic condition managed and explicitly documented, with stroke-risk counseling around anticoagulation interruption.

differential.diagnosis: Chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction with peripheral volume overload
supporting_evidence: HFpEF listed; cardiologist recently increased Lasix
Moderate bilateral pitting edema on admission exam, mild at discharge
Lasix held periprocedurally then restarted
opposing_evidence: No dyspnea, lungs clear, no hypoxia this stay
differential.reasoning: Edema and active diuretic titration support a coded chronic HFpEF diagnosis, though no acute decompensation occurred.

supporting_evidence: Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, baseline documented 1.6–1.8
Home calcitriol continued
Prior ICD-10 N183
opposing_evidence: Creatinine actually better than baseline this stay
differential.reasoning: Documented chronic renal impairment managed during the stay; relevant to fluids, contrast, and drug dosing.

differential.diagnosis: Essential hypertension with hypertensive heart disease
supporting_evidence: BP 142/57 on admission
Continued propranolol, lisinopril, amlodipine
Prior ICD-10 I110
opposing_evidence: No hypertensive urgency or end-organ event this stay
differential.reasoning: Stable chronic hypertension actively treated with three agents; supports comorbidity coding.

differential.diagnosis: Recurrent/resolved ascending cholangitis following prior biliary stenting
supporting_evidence: Prior admission principal diagnosis was cholangitis with stent placement
Periprocedural ciprofloxacin given
opposing_evidence: Afebrile, WBC 7.2, normal LFTs and bilirubin
differential.reasoning: Historical context only; current labs and exam show no active biliary infection, so scored low.

supporting_evidence: Sphincterotomy performed with anticoagulation recently held
Slight tenderness bilateral upper abdomen
opposing_evidence: Procedure described as uncomplicated; tolerating regular diet
differential.reasoning: Standard post-ERCP complications were monitored for but not documented; low likelihood given benign course.

rule_outs.why: Afebrile, WBC 7.2, normal bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase, no antibiotics continued.
No abdominal pain, tolerating regular diet, discharged next day.
No dyspnea or hypoxia, clear lungs; edema only, Lasix restarted at discharge.
Creatinine 1.4 is below documented baseline of 1.6–1.8.

uncertain_areas: Whether the ERCP report designates stones in the common bile duct versus gallbladder only
Lipase/amylase values post-procedure to exclude subclinical pancreatitis
Documented ejection fraction and whether HFpEF was coded acute vs chronic
Whether cholecystitis was present on any current imaging (none recorded)
